method: Second-nearby NYMEX WTI holding return over each contract cycle (roll-free), carry = (C1 - C2) / C2 on the first day after expiry, long when carry exceeds the median of all prior months, else flat. Non-overlapping monthly windows.
data: EIA RCLC1/RCLC2 daily settlements (series discontinued after 2024-04-05)

field_notes.mean_ret_backwardated_pct: legacy alias of mean_ret_above_median_carry_pct: the rule's split on the median of prior months' carry, NOT the sign of carry (see sign_split)
field_notes.mean_ret_contango_pct: legacy alias of mean_ret_below_median_carry_pct: the rule's split on the median of prior months' carry, NOT the sign of carry (see sign_split)
field_notes.n_backwardated: legacy alias of n_above_median_carry: the rule's split on the median of prior months' carry, NOT the sign of carry (see sign_split)
field_notes.sharpe_difference: carry-timed minus buy-and-hold Sharpe, annualized; Ledoit-Wolf (2008) HAC delta method and a stationary block bootstrap, two-sided

sign_split.definition: carry > 0 (backwardation) vs carry <= 0 (contango); long when carry > 0

power_post_2007.statement: After 2007 (206 months) the spread test could only detect a spread of 3.47%/month or more (one-sided 5%, 80% power); it had 67% power against the pre-2007 spread of 2.92%/month, so a null spread there is weak evidence of decay. The rank test could detect a correlation of 0.178 and had 89% power against the pre-2007 rank correlation of 0.204.

roll_bias_of_original_method.note: Original design: unadjusted contract-1 (== CL=F) 21-day forward returns. On the same dates the roll gap subtracts roughly the carry itself.

verdict: Months with carry above its prior-months median beat the rest significantly over the full sample (one-sided p = 0.018); the true sign split (backwardation vs contango) agrees (p = 0.015). After 2007 the spread is not distinguishable from zero (p = 0.27), but that test had only 67% power against the pre-2007 spread and the pre/post spread difference is not significant (p = 0.26); the rank correlation, with 89% power, fell from 0.20 to -0.03 (difference p = 0.0210). The Sharpe gain of timing over buy-and-hold is not significant (Ledoit-Wolf p = 0.11 full sample, 0.57 after 2007), and as a sign predictor it does not beat always-long over the full sample. No reliable modern-era edge is demonstrated; how much of the pre-2007 effect survives is not resolved by this sample.
